filled_passage:
Our reading club meets in a small room on Wednesdays. We bring our own books, so everyone can read something they enjoy. We do not all have to finish the same story.

The first ten minutes are silent. Nobody talks, and we put our phones away. Then we sit in a circle. A student may tell us about a favourite character, but should not tell the ending if others still want to read the book.

You can also bring a page you do not understand. We try to help, but the club is not a test. There are no marks. It is fine to ask a simple question.

Last month, Ben brought a book of poems. He was afraid no one would listen. When he began reading, we all became quiet. Afterwards, three students asked to borrow his book. We wrote our names on a list to decide the order.

Sometimes a member forgets a book. There are a few on the shelf for anyone to use. Before leaving, we put the chairs around the table again. The room is ready for the afternoon class, and we leave with new ideas about what to read next.
